newsitem.title: USA: Central Maine results seen below averages.
newsitem.headline: Central Maine results seen below averages.

text.p: Central Maine Power Co's 1997 results will be substantially below industry averages, President David T. Flanagan said Thursday.
He told the annual meeting expenses from the utility's 38 percent share of Maine Yankee Atomic Power Co and other nuclear investments "will bear down on CMP's financial results" for 1997.
"Because we must hold the line on price increases to meet customer expectations, those results will be substantially below industry averages," he said.

Noting announced preparations to offer the company's generating plants for sale, Flanagan said: "The prospect of exiting the generating business, the need to reinvest earnings for growth and the financial pressures from our nuclear investments clearly require examining the appropriateness of the current (dividend) policy."
Central Maine last paid $0.225 per share on April 30 a continuation of the quarterly rate paid the past two years.
The company noted sale of its generating plants would be required by the utility restructuring bill now before the Maine legislature.
If able to arrange a sale, Central Maine said, it would use temporary lease-back or buy-back arrangements to continue meeting customers' power needs until the onset of retail competition.
